newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Growing market can absorb olive oil glut - officials.
newsitem.headline: Growing market can absorb olive oil glut - officials.

text.p: Growing markets in North America, Asia and northern Europe could absorb a glut in olive oil production, officials at a conference in Lisbon said on Monday.

Asked to comment on the impact of falling olive oil prices for the industry, Fausto Luchetti, executive director of the International Olive Oil Council (IOC), said: "I don't think this is bad news. Because there is room for consumption."
Speaking on the sidelines of a four-day IOC conference, he added: "We are dealing with the expansion of consumption in South East Asia, Japan, and in America."
Olive oil prices have been falling sharply since last September.
The IOC said last week that global olive oil output could surge by 38 percent in 1996/97 compared with 1995/96, and prices would fall further this year.
Global production could reach 2.261 million tonnes in 1996/97, of which 70 percent would come from the European Union.
The IOC conference, which opened on Monday, brought together representatives from 24 countries responsible for 93 percent of the world's olive oil production.
Luchetti said it was vital to inform consumers around the world that olive oil was a healthy product so that demand would increase.
"Our major objective is to educate the consumer about the health properties of olive oil," he told Reuters.
"It is very important to satisfy health-conscious consumers," added Luchetti, whose group defends the interests of producers.

In an opening speech to the conference, Portuguese Agriculture Minister Fernando Gomes da Silva said his country sought to boost olive oil production as the industry had strong potential to satisfy demand by consumers at home and abroad.
"The prospects of world markets, namely in northern Europe, Asia and America, clearly encourage increased production," he said.
The minister said production of olive oil in Portugal satisfied half the needs of domestic consumption, as well as providing some exports.
He hoped that annual consumption per capita in Portugal would rise to 10 kg per capita from around five kg now as domestic production increased.
